SuttaCentral lists five translations of the work in five different modern languages, but records no curated historical parallels in other Buddhist traditions [SuttaCentral].

The text also shares recurrent apadāna poetic units with other Therāpadāna poems, most prominently with another homonymous poem, *Pāpanivāriyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 222, notably segments §6.2–10.1), as well as the *Kapparukkhiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 42), *Pañcaṅguliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 172), and *Yūthikapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 202) [DharmaNexus]. An automatic machine alignment is also registered with the Tibetan version of the *Pratyutpannabuddhasaṃmukhāvasthitasamādhisūtra* (D0133), though it has a low plausibility score and is not confirmed as an established parallel by SuttaCentral [DharmaNexus].
